work_atc.tut.card.title: Air traffic control tutorial
work_atc.tut.server.aircraft_failed: The tutorial aircraft could not be created, the tutorial ends.
work_atc.tut.server.aircraft_lost: The tutorial aircraft was removed, a new one comes.
work_atc.tut.server.cannot_start_now: You cannot start the tutorial now.
work_atc.tut.server.completed: Tutorial completed. Have a good shift!
work_atc.tut.server.could_not_start: The tutorial could not be started.
work_atc.tut.server.ended_died: The tutorial ended because you died.
work_atc.tut.server.log_out_first: Log out of your ATC position first.
work_atc.tut.server.logged_out_early: You logged out before the end. Log in again at the console ({console}).
work_atc.tut.server.no_problem: No problem. You can start the tutorial any time with /{command}.
work_atc.tut.server.skipped: Tutorial skipped. You can start it again with /{command}.
work_atc.tut.server.system_not_running: The air traffic control system is not running, the tutorial cannot go on.
work_atc.tut.steps.air_leave: Your sector is the CTR of {airport}: the ground, the runway and a strip of air around it. The tower does not give a departure levels or headings: it got its initial level with the IFR clearance, and only approach (APP) climbs it further. When {dep} leaves the CTR, it belongs to approach; approach is closed now, so the pilots fly their flight plan alone and the label turns grey.
work_atc.tut.steps.air_wait: {dep} is rolling. After take-off it flies the runway heading up to 800 ft above the field, then its SID, and climbs to the initial level.
work_atc.tut.steps.alerts_emrg: The red EMRG above the label is an alert: {arr} squawks 7700, an emergency. Others: COMS = 7600 radio failure, DUPE = two aircraft with the same squawk, STCA = separation loss, RAM = the aircraft left its route.
work_atc.tut.steps.alerts_fines: Separation losses are fined, but only in your own sector: two ground aircraft head-on {gnd}; closer than 0.1 nm and 1000 ft in a TMA {tma}, in the CTA {cta}. Fines are taken from your pay, even when the total is negative.
work_atc.tut.steps.alerts_logout: Press Logout in the top right corner. In the tutorial nothing is paid, you only see the receipt.
work_atc.tut.steps.alerts_pay:
You are paid when you log out: {per_action} for every accepted command, more the longer you stay (+{bonus}% per minute, at most x{max}), and {per_aircraft} for every aircraft you controlled. Every command also gives work XP.

You start as a tower controller; approach (APP) comes at level {app}, radar (centre) at level {radar}.
work_atc.tut.steps.arr_land: {arr} comes from approach (APP), already cleared for the approach: it flies to the final fix and on to the runway. Its label is grey until it reaches your CTR / the final; then it is yours and asks for the landing clearance (LAND, yellow). Give Cleared to land before it is 400 m from the threshold, otherwise it goes around.
work_atc.tut.steps.arr_parked: {arr} taxies to the stand. Wait until it parks.
work_atc.tut.steps.arr_taxi: {arr} has landed. Off the runway it asks for taxi: Taxi to stand > any free stand, or a named one.
work_atc.tut.steps.arr_vacate:
With Vacate via > you can name the runway exit; without it the pilots take the first one towards the terminal. Go around sends it round again if the runway is not free.

Wait for the landing.
work_atc.tut.steps.arr_wait: An arrival ({arr}) is coming on the final of runway {arr_rwy}...
work_atc.tut.steps.console_login:
The login window lists the positions of this console. You start as a tower controller ({position}): the tower controls the aircraft on the ground, on the runway and in the CTR around the airport.

Click Log in.
work_atc.tut.steps.console_walk:
You are in the operations room of San Andreas Control. Every ATC position is opened here; the airport towers have no consoles.

Walk into the blue marker of the {airport} consoles and press {console}.
work_atc.tut.steps.delivery_ifr: First the IFR clearance: in the menu choose IFR clearance >, then the departure procedure (SID). The yellow one is suggested: it starts the filed route from the runway in use. Then the initial level: 3000 ft is the standard.
work_atc.tut.steps.delivery_push: Cleared! The label now asks for PUSH. Open the menu again and choose Pushback approved.
work_atc.tut.steps.delivery_pushing: {dep} is pushed back tail first onto the taxiway, nose towards the runway. When it stops, it asks for taxi (TAXI).
work_atc.tut.steps.done_text:
In short:
1. Go on duty, then the console in the SA Control room: {console}, Log in.
2. Departures: IFR clearance, Pushback, Taxi, Take-off; leaving the CTR they go to approach.
3. Arrivals (from approach): Cleared to land, Taxi to stand.
4. Yellow = they ask, red = alert. Watch the separation.
5. Logout pays.

Read the documents on sanandreascontrol.eu (in-game browser): NAV, SW, OPS, then LOA.
/{command}: the tutorial again.
work_atc.tut.steps.ground_rules:
While taxiing: aircraft keep 60 m behind each other in a queue, and nobody enters a runway without your clearance: they stop before it (holding short) and ask.

Two aircraft facing each other on a taxiway is a separation loss (a fine) - plan the taxi routes.
work_atc.tut.steps.ground_takeoff:
It holds short and asks (yellow in the menu): CROSS = Cross runway; BKTRK = Backtrack runway (it rolls to the threshold on the runway and turns round); T/O = Line up and wait or Cleared for take-off. Take-off clearance is accepted only at the runway.

Clear {dep} for take-off.
work_atc.tut.steps.ground_taxi: Choose Taxi > and the runway: the one in use ({dep_rwy}) is marked. The pilots find the way on the taxiways by themselves.
work_atc.tut.steps.label_air:
Airborne labels are longer: callsign + controller, type / wake; altitude in hundreds of feet (045 = 4500 ft), speed, destination; the cleared level (when set); the waypoint or heading; squawk (on hover) and vertical speed. A grey label is not yours.

You can drag a label with the left mouse button; right click on it shows its route.
work_atc.tut.steps.label_ground:
{dep} is at its stand. A ground label shows the callsign, the speed and the squawk code, then the type and the wake category. The colour tells departure or arrival.

A yellow frame means it asks you for something now.
work_atc.tut.steps.label_menu: Click the label of {dep}: the command menu opens.
work_atc.tut.steps.label_menu_info: At the top is the flight: type, route, procedure, who controls it. Below are the commands in groups. On the ground the whole flow is listed in order: only the step it is at now can be clicked, the rest is grey. Yellow = what the pilots ask for.
work_atc.tut.steps.label_wait: A departure ({dep}) is coming to a stand of {airport}...
work_atc.tut.steps.note_fast: Fast forward x{scale}: nobody is waiting for you.
work_atc.tut.steps.note_go_around: It went around: it flies the go-around procedure (GA) up to 3000 ft and comes back for a new approach. Clear it again (approach, then landing).
work_atc.tut.steps.note_open_console: Stand in the console marker and press {console}.
work_atc.tut.steps.note_open_scope: The scope is hidden: press {console} at the console marker.
work_atc.tut.steps.offer:
Would you like a short tutorial? You will control a departure and an arrival as a tower controller, with nobody else's traffic around. It takes about 15 minutes, and you can skip it any time.

/{command} starts it later.
work_atc.tut.steps.scope_buttons: List: on/off hides the lists, Reset view brings the map back. Hide closes the scope but you stay logged in ({console} at the console shows it again). Logout ends the session and pays you (not now, it comes at the end).
work_atc.tut.steps.scope_intro:
This is the radar scope of {position}. You look at the airspace from above: the CTR of {airport} around the runways, the TMA of the approach around it, fixes (triangles), the runways, and later the aircraft.

In the tutorial only your own two aircraft fly here.
work_atc.tut.steps.scope_list: On the right are the Departures and Arrivals of your airport. Your aircraft are blue. When an aircraft asks you for something, its ALT column shows REQ in yellow. Clicking a row centres the map on it.
work_atc.tut.steps.scope_tools: AT shows / hides the names of the airspaces, FIXL the fix names. V- / V+ (or the keys 0-5) set the length of the speed vector ahead of every airborne aircraft.
work_atc.tut.steps.scope_topbar: The top bar shows your position and the runways in use: ARR = landing runway, DEP = take-off runway (now {arr_rwy} / {dep_rwy}), then the wind (from where, knots). The runways follow the wind.
work_atc.tut.steps.scope_view: Mouse wheel: zoom where the cursor is. Right mouse button held: move the map. Taxiways, stands and ground traffic appear only when you zoom in. Distances are in nautical miles (scale bar), altitudes in feet, speeds in knots.
